data.description:
# Raise llama-server numbered-log retention for multi-day post-deploy measurement windows

Discovered from: LP-0MV5HSZ51005CM7A (40,960 MiB cache-ram validation).

## Problem

`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` keeps only the 15 most
recent llama-server restart segments. The prompt-cache post-deploy validation
(AC2 of LP-0MV5HSZ51005CM7A) requires a ~4.7-day / ~1,400-request window, but
with the current restart rate (mode-switch fast<->cheap restarts, crash
restarts; 15+ segments cycled within a single day) the window's early data is
discarded as it accrues. The surviving 40,960 MiB corpus *shrank* across
captures (1,065 req on 2026-10-16 07:16 -> 760 on 21:44 -> 380 on
2026-10-18), and the saturated/high-eviction segments were among those lost,
biasing the fragment toward short cold-cache segments.

## Options (to decide)

1. Raise `keep` (e.g. 60) — cheap but only postpones the problem.
2. Archive daily llama-server logs into the daily `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`
   stream (logrotate safety-net already exists; ensure it runs while the
   in-process numbered rotation also operates) so a window is always
   reconstructible from dated files.
3. Have the measurement script snapshot the corpus (copy/archive) at each
   capture so interim artifacts stay reproducible.

## Acceptance criteria

- A ~4.7-day post-deploy prompt-cache window can be reconstructed from
  surviving logs after the fact (no count shrinkage across captures).
- Documented in HOST_INSTALL / log-rotation docs; not a load-bearing change
  to prompt-cache behaviour.
data.title: Raise llama-server numbered-log retention for multi-day post-deploy measurement windows
